guideposts.label: The 3rd country of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: After Monaco and France, it’s time for Andorran racing. As of tomorrow, La Vuelta will settle in Spain, the fourth country on this edition’s route. The race visited four countries last year too: Italy, France, Andorra, and Spain.

guideposts.label: Andorra la Vella, a classic of La Vuelta
guideposts.detail: Andorra la Vella is a classic of La Vuelta since the Spanish Grand Tour first ventured in Andorra, in 1965. On day 11, the race went from Barcelona to Andorra la Vella, passing Collada de Toses and Port d’Envalira. Spain’s Esteban Martin won the stage and Rolf Wolfshohl retained the overall lead, en route to success a week later in Bilbao. The last La Vuelta stage winner in Andorra la Vella is Vin

guideposts.label: Good memories for Kuss and Skjelmose
guideposts.detail: In 2021, the Tour de France also had a stage finish in Andorra la Vella, after summiting Port d’Envalira and Collada de Beixalis. Sepp Kuss took what remains the last USA Tour stage win to date. Since 2025, Andorra la Vella is the start of the Andorra MoraBanc Classica. guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: UAE Emirates XRG still lead the team standings with a gap of 3’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike and 23’’ to Netcompany Ineos.

guideposts.label: Uriarte attacks, UAE already control
guideposts.detail: Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) has opened a gap after 1 kilometre of racing. A Tadej Pogacar teammate (Ivo Oliveira?) sets the pace at the front of the peloton.

guideposts.label: Attacking towards the highest summit of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: At 2,409 metres of altitude, Port d’Envalira is the highest summit of La Vuelta 26. The other 2,000+ summit of this edition is Calar Alto (2,153m), the finish of stage 12. Already passed during the first La Vuelta stage in Andorra (1965), Port d’Envalira has often featured in the Spanish Grand Tour, as well as the Tour de France and also the Volta a Catalunya. guideposts.label: A dozen riders on the move
guideposts.detail: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) and a dozen more attackers want to get away on the first slopes up Port d'Envalira.

guideposts.label: Around 40 riders on the move
guideposts.detail: We can see Matthew Brennan, Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike), Ivan Romeo (Movistar), Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla), Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious)... UAE Emirates XRG drive the bunch a handful of seconds behind.

guideposts.label: Uijtdebroeks among the early stragglers
guideposts.detail: The Belgian climber is affected by his crash on day 1.

guideposts.label: The battle goes on
guideposts.detail: At km 9, eight riders try to get away after the peloton caught the large group on the move. Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) is up there.

guideposts.label: Visma vs UAE
guideposts.detail: After 17 kilometres, the gap is up to 1 minute, with Visma-Lease a Bike driving the breakaway and UAE Emirates XRG pulling the bunch. Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) is dropped from the breakaway as his teammate Jan Hirt joins the front group. Sergio Samitier (Cofidis) and Mario Aparicio (Burgos Burpellet BH) are also bridging the gap. guideposts.label: Armirail returns to the front group
guideposts.detail: The last gap to the bunch: 37 seconds.

guideposts.label: Double accelerates inside the final kilometre of ascent
guideposts.detail: The break explodes. And so does the bunch.

guideposts.label: Fortunato coquers the Port d'Envalira
guideposts.detail: Double opened the sprint but the Italian climber passed him at the summit.

guideposts.detail: In 2021, Patrick Konrad (Lidl-Trek) won a Tour de France stage starting from Pas de la Casa, also featured on today’s route (km 29.9): “I have really good memories. A victory at the Tour is something every cyclist dreams about and I’m also really proud of it. Today, I go very motivated into the stage. I love Andorra to prepare big races in altitude.
